category_title: Verbal students with autism who fluctuate between disengagement and disruptive or flirtatious behavior
scenario_title: Independent academic tasks and peer interaction in general education classes
minimal_context: Maya is in her general education Spanish class and is expected to complete an independent academic task by initiating a conversation with a classmate.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Maya, it is time for the independent academic task in Spanish class. Please practice talking with your classmate.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Engages in repetitive handling of objects and skin picking) In Spanish, yes, talk Spanish and learn new things.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: That is correct. Go ahead and start the conversation with him.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Puts her head down on her desk and does not initiate conversation with the classmate without disabilities)

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Maya, please lift your head up and do the task.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Lifts her head and suddenly shouts an order at the male classmate while engaging in repetitive hand and finger movements) Sit down right now!

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: Maya, it is time for the independent academic task in Spanish class. Please practice talking with your classmate.

STUDENT: (Engages in repetitive handling of objects and skin picking) In Spanish, yes, talk Spanish and learn new things.

TUTOR: That is correct. Go ahead and start the conversation with him.

STUDENT: (Puts her head down on her desk and does not initiate conversation with the classmate without disabilities)

TUTOR: Maya, please lift your head up and do the task.

STUDENT: (Lifts her head and suddenly shouts an order at the male classmate while engaging in repetitive hand and finger movements) Sit down right now!

task.content: Independent academic tasks and social interaction periods where the student is expected to talk and learn new things (e.g., talk Spanish and learn new things)
task.learning_goal: Initiate and reciprocate conversation with classmates without disabilities

context.environment: General education classes including Spanish, US history, and business management
context.materials: Small, handheld, bound pages or cards containing a typed conversational opener with a corresponding Picture Communication Symbol®
context.social_setting: Classmates without disabilities and two female peers who were in her special education classes

challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Often put her head down on her desk; engaged in repetitive stereotypic behavior, including hand and finger movements, eye rubbing, verbal stereotypy, repetitive handling of objects, and skin picking
related_quotes: In Spanish, yes, talk Spanish and learn new things. In US history, just talk. In business management, I talk to two people: P____ and B____.

behavior_patterns.condition: Occasionally during class when typically quiet
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Engaged in disruptive behavior at which time she would shout orders at peers or act overtly flirtatious with male students
